messages:
alex: :rotating_light: infra-bot alerted — 3 nodes in infer-pool became NotReady in the last 2m, looks like kubelet restarted
incident-bot: Incident detected 2026-03-15T16:25:00Z — elevated 5xx on /v1/generate (us-west), auto-paging oncall
maya: I'm on call, joining. pulling metrics and k8s events now
ben: seeing tail latency spike and 503s up to ~6% for infer-pool-usw, errors concentrated on gpu-backed routes
sre-larry: kube events: kubelet process exit on inf-node-03/04/07 — suspected OOM/kubelet restart loop
naomi: grabbing node journal from inf-node-03: `kubectl -n kube-system logs kubelet inf-node-03 --tail=200`
alex: paste of journal snippets:
```
Mar 15 16:22:09 inf-node-03 kubelet[1234]: runtime: out of memory: cannot allocate 64MB
Mar 15 16:22:10 inf-node-03 kubelet[1234]: SIGKILL (oom-killer) invoked
Mar 15 16:22:11 inf-node-03 systemd[1]: kubelet.service: Main process exited, code=killed, status=9/KILL
Mar 15 16:22:13 inf-node-03 systemd[1]: Stopped kubelet.
```
maya: also seeing serving pod logs prior to kubelet death with CUDA errors + OOMs — possible driver/alloc mismatch
ben: example from model pod on the node:
```
E cuda: cuCtxCreate failed: CUDA_ERROR_INVALID_DEVICE
E serving: kv-cache failed to mmap
E runtime: OOM allocating 1.2GB for attention layer
```
naomi: traffic report shows ~30% of requests routed to CPU fallback variants due to immediate rescheduling -> explains latency jump
sre-larry: immediate mitigation: cordon inf-node-03/04/07 to prevent more pods landing. doing now.
alex: ran `kubectl cordon inf-node-03 inf-node-04 inf-node-07` — nodes cordoned
maya: draining pods on those nodes with grace 10s to speed reschedule: `kubectl drain inf-node-03 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data --grace-period=10`
ben: autoscaler reacted and spun new nodes but I see some came up with gpu-driver:v2025.11 while runtime expects v2026.02 — driver image mismatch on booted nodes
naomi: confirmed via cloud-init logs: new instances received an older driver AMI tag, likely an image pipeline race during recent AMI roll
sre-larry: switching routing policy to prefer warm dedicated fallback pool in another AZ to pull traffic off us-west problem nodes — kicking warm-up
alex: updating routing rules: `PATCH /routing/policies/infer-pool` -> enable cross-az fallback, reduce stickiness
incident-bot: PagerDuty: alert escalated to maya -> ben -> naomi
maya: handing primary to ben for infra remediation; I'll keep monitoring latency and customer impact
ben: plan (short):
- pin autoscaler to previous AMI tag to stop bad nodes from joining
- cordon new bad nodes and mark for rebuild
- coordinate AMI rebuild with infra to include correct gpu-driver
- restart kubelet on affected nodes after driver load
naomi: temporary app-level mitigations: reduce model batch-size and disable KV prefix caching to lower memory footprint — rolling config now
alex: applying config change to model-configs: `max_batch_tokens: 512`, `kv_cache_enabled: false` — rolling update started
ben: infra started AMI rebuild with correct driver (starting bake), ETA ~25m; I'll post AMI id when ready
sre-larry: compiling customer impact list: Vidly (vid-42) reporting 30% increased latency, ChatCo experiencing intermittent errors — drafting status update for customers
maya: incident severity set to sev2 — customer-facing but partial fallback mitigations active
alex: status page draft: "Investigating: subset of inference nodes in US-WEST experienced kubelet restarts due to memory pressure combined with a GPU driver mismatch on newly provisioned nodes. Traffic is being routed to fallback pools while we roll back and rebuild the AMI. Engineers are working on a fix; some customers may see increased latency and intermittent errors."
ben: rolled back autoscaler group tag and cordoned remaining new nodes to halt bad boots
naomi: kernel excerpt from a healthy node after rollback:
```
Mar 15 16:44:01 inf-node-08 kernel: NVRM: GPU at PCI:0000:65:00: GPU-0: process XXXXX killed due to OOM
Mar 15 16:44:02 inf-node-08 nvidia: NvHost: driver reinit
```
maya: latency trending down — currently ~1.8x baseline, 5xx at ~0.6% (was 6%)
ben: next: once AMI baked I'll patch nodes, restart kubelet on inf-node-03/04/07: `systemctl restart kubelet` and monitor pod reschedule/health
alex: handoff — ben you're primary. @ben you're on pagerduty primary now
ben: ack, taking it. will post live updates here.
incident-bot: Next scheduled oncall rotation in 30m
naomi: post-incident action items to file:
- add driver compatibility gate to autoscaler pipeline (prevent AMI with mismatched drivers)
- add kubelet/cgroup memory guard to avoid kubelet OOM under pressure
- add serving config guardrails (batching/kvcache thresholds)
- add chaos test simulating node boot + driver mismatch
maya: agreed, filing Jira tickets and tagging eng-infra + eng-runtime
alex: thanks all. we'll keep the thread open until kubelet restarts confirmed and latency near baseline
ben: update 16:52Z — AMI baked with gpu-driver:v2026.02-fixed (ami-0b7f1234). rolling nodes now
ben: update 17:01Z — nodes rejoined, kubelet restarted cleanly on inf-node-03/04/07, pods rescheduled. 5xx down to 0.1%, latency ~1.05x baseline
maya: closing incident in 10m if metrics remain stable. I'll post RCA to postmortems channel and link Jira
reaction notes: :thumbsup: from eng-oncall, :eyes: from product
